title: Marking updates with useTransition

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Marking updates with useTransition

children.text: A transition marks an update as interruptible, so typing stays smooth while an expensive list re-filters behind it.
What this lesson covers
Separate an urgent update from a non-urgent one
Show pending state without blocking input
Recognise the interactions worth marking
This lesson sits in Concurrent React, part of React Performance Engineering. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Separate an urgent update from a non-urgent one
Show pending state without blocking input
Recognise the interactions worth marking

title: Deferring expensive values

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Deferring expensive values

children.text: A deferred value lags behind the real one on purpose, letting the urgent render finish first with the previous result.
What this lesson covers
Defer a value that drives expensive rendering
Choose between deferring a value and wrapping an update
Communicate staleness to the user while it catches up
This lesson sits in Concurrent React, part of React Performance Engineering. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Defer a value that drives expensive rendering
Choose between deferring a value and wrapping an update
Communicate staleness to the user while it catches up

title: Suspense for data loading

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Suspense for data loading

children.text: Suspense moves loading state out of the component and into its boundary, so you stop threading isLoading through the tree.
What this lesson covers
Place boundaries where a meaningful fallback exists
Avoid a single boundary that blocks the whole page
Combine Suspense with error boundaries for failures
This lesson sits in Concurrent React, part of React Performance Engineering. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Place boundaries where a meaningful fallback exists
Avoid a single boundary that blocks the whole page
Combine Suspense with error boundaries for failures
proTip: Put the boundary where a skeleton would make sense to a user, not wherever the fetch happens to live.

title: Code splitting that pays off

children.text: Splitting only helps if the split-off code was genuinely not needed for the first screen. Analyse the bundle before you cut it.

title: Lazy loading and prefetching

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Lazy loading and prefetching

children.text: Lazy loading defers the download; prefetching starts it early on a hint like hover. Together they hide the network cost from the user.
What this lesson covers
Load a component only when it is about to be needed
Prefetch on intent signals such as hover or viewport
Keep a fallback that does not shift the layout
This lesson sits in Bundle and Load Performance, part of React Performance Engineering. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Load a component only when it is about to be needed
Prefetch on intent signals such as hover or viewport
Keep a fallback that does not shift the layout

Reserve space so images do not shift the layout
Choose a font loading strategy that avoids invisible text

Reserve space so images do not shift the layout
Choose a font loading strategy that avoids invisible text

title: Structural typing and assignability

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Structural typing and assignability

children.text: TypeScript compares shapes, not names. Two unrelated types are interchangeable if their members line up, which explains most surprising assignability errors.
What this lesson covers
Compare types by structure rather than declaration
Read an assignability error from the mismatched member up
Use branded types when structural compatibility is too loose
This lesson sits in How the Type System Thinks, part of TypeScript for Application Developers. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Compare types by structure rather than declaration
Read an assignability error from the mismatched member up
Use branded types when structural compatibility is too loose

title: Unions and narrowing

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Unions and narrowing

children.text: A discriminated union plus a check on the discriminant is the workhorse pattern of typed application code. Narrowing is how the compiler follows your control flow.
What this lesson covers
Model alternatives as a discriminated union
Narrow with typeof, in, and discriminant checks
Make a switch exhaustive with a never assertion
This lesson sits in How the Type System Thinks, part of TypeScript for Application Developers. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Model alternatives as a discriminated union
Narrow with typeof, in, and discriminant checks
Make a switch exhaustive with a never assertion
proTip: An exhaustive switch that assigns the leftover case to never turns a future missing branch into a compile error.

title: Literal types and const assertions
